title: Inscribe is one of the first document fraud detection vendors to be ISO 42001 certified
summary: Inscribe is now ISO 42001 certified. Here's what the AI management standard covers and why it matters when you choose a fraud detection vendor.
body_markdown:
If a vendor's AI plays a part in your decisions, you should know how it's governed.


Banks, credit unions, fintechs, and lenders are asking that question more often. Until recently, there was no standard way to answer it. Vendors described their own practices, and buyers had to take their word for it.


ISO 42001 (formally ISO/IEC 42001:2023) changes that. It's the first international standard for managing AI, and it is verified by an independent audit. Inscribe has been awarded an ISO 42001 certification.


### What is ISO 42001?


ISO 42001 is the international standard for an AI management system, published in December 2023. It sets out how an organization should govern the AI it builds and uses, from how it manages risk to who is accountable.


It's new, and few vendors have it. About 270 certificates had been issued worldwide by the end of 2025, compared with roughly 125,000 for ISO 27001. Having it means a vendor got ahead of AI governance before most of the market. Inscribe is among the first wave of companies to earn it.


### How is it different from SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001?


You may already ask vendors for SOC 2 or ISO 27001. Those cover information security, like protecting data, access and encryption, threat management, and security incidents.


ISO 42001 covers something different. It's focused on an AIMS (AI Management System) and ensuring responsible use of AI. It looks at how we use data, which AI systems we use, and whether we use them fairly. That includes transparency, human oversight of AI, and AI impact checks.


ISO 42001 has a lot in common with both ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type 2. They all rely on an independent audit every year, a risk-based approach, clear accountability, and ongoing improvement. The standard also requires defined roles inside the company. ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type 2 show your data is secured. ISO 42001 shows the AI working with it is governed.


### What did the audit look at?


In September, external auditors came in for the first time to audit our AIMS against the standard. An accredited third-party auditor reviewed our documented controls for building, testing, monitoring, and improving AI, and approved the system for certification.


The standard also requires an external audit every year.


### Why does this matter when you're choosing a vendor?


Vendor reviews take time, and security questionnaires keep getting longer. AI questions are now part of them.


A certification doesn't replace your own due diligence, but it gives you a head start. You get independent verification of how a vendor governs AI instead of the vendor's own description. It also shows that we've looked closely at how we use AI. It can ease due diligence reviews and questionnaires, and it supports alignment with regulations like the EU AI Act.


### What to ask any AI vendor


Whether or not a vendor is certified, these questions are worth asking.


1. How do you test for bias?
2. Where does a person review the AI's work?
3. Who is accountable for it?
4. How do you find out when something goes wrong?
5. Who checks your answers?


ISO 42001 gives vendors a structured way to answer all five.


### What it means for how we build


AI is doing more of the work in fraud prevention, so how it's built matters as much as what it catches. ISO 42001 means an independent auditor has reviewed how we build, test, monitor, and improve ours, against the transparency, human oversight, and safeguards financial institutions should expect from a vendor. We're one of the first document fraud detection vendors to have it.
